subtopic: Decomposition of ATen ops in torch.compile
learningObjective: Identify the purpose and effect of ATen op decomposition in PyTorch 2's compile stack.
stem: PyTorch 2's compile stack applies 'decompositions' that rewrite higher-level ATen ops into simpler primitive ops before Inductor codegen. Which statements about this decomposition are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Decomposition is performed in the AOTAutograd/pre-Inductor stage over the traced FX graph, before Inductor's scheduler and codegen phases.
Every ATen op is always fully decomposed to elementwise ops; there are no exceptions such as `matmul`, `convolution`, or attention that remain opaque to Inductor.
Decomposition rules are user-extensible: users can register a decomposition for a custom op to make it lowerable by Inductor without changing Inductor internals.
Decomposition reduces the effective op vocabulary Inductor must generate code for; composite ops (e.g., `nn.functional.layer_norm`) are rewritten into simpler primitives (mul, add, sqrt, mean, etc.).

explanation: A: decomposition shrinks the op vocabulary Inductor must handle. B: it runs before Inductor codegen (typically in AOTAutograd's decomposition table application). D: users can extend the decomposition table for custom ops to make them lowerable. C is wrong: many ops (matmul, convolution, attention) remain as high-level ops and are handled by Inductor's specialized paths or by ATen fallbacks, not decomposed all the way to elementwise primitives.

optionExplanations.B: Wrong: matmul/convolution/attention are commonly preserved for kernel selection.

assumptions: The user has not overridden the decomposition table with an incompatible custom set.
nonImplications: Does not imply that every decomposition is faster; sometimes the composite form has a better hand-written kernel.
Does not imply decompositions are unique; different pipelines may choose different decomps for the same op.

distractorRationales.B: Wrong claim of complete elementwise decomposition for all ops.
